limitations: Pattern-based static review of text files only; no data-flow or taint analysis.
Source-pattern matches are reported as 'potential' unless the evidence itself is conclusive (for example a token format or an explicit unsafe setting).
A match on a secret format shows the format, not that the credential is live. No credential was tested.
Git history, dependencies, advisories, running systems and remote cloud state were not inspected.
Absence of findings is not evidence of security.

findings.title: pull_request_target workflow checks out pull-request code
findings.description: A workflow triggered by `pull_request_target` runs with repository secrets and a write token. Checking out the PR head and then running its code lets an outside contributor execute code with those privileges.
findings.remediation: Use `pull_request` for untrusted code. If `pull_request_target` is required, do not check out or execute PR-controlled content, and keep permissions minimal.
findings.falsePositives: Workflows that check out the PR head but never build, run or source it (for example, labelling only).
findings.verification: Confirm no step after the checkout executes files from the PR head, or remove the head checkout.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Untrusted GitHub context interpolated into a shell step
findings.description: Attacker-controlled fields (PR title/body, branch name, issue or comment text) are expanded directly inside a `run:` script. A crafted value can inject shell commands.
findings.remediation: Pass the value through an environment variable (`env: TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}`) and reference it as `"$TITLE"` in the script.
findings.falsePositives: Fields restricted by GitHub to safe characters. Only matches inside run blocks are reported when detectable; verify context.
findings.verification: The expression no longer appears inside a `run:` body.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Pod shares host network, PID or IPC namespace
findings.description: hostNetwork, hostPID or hostIPC removes namespace isolation between the pod and the node.
findings.remediation: Remove the host namespace flags unless the workload is a vetted node agent.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Kubernetes container runs privileged
findings.description: `privileged: true` gives the container nearly all host capabilities and device access, so a container escape is trivial.
findings.remediation: Remove `privileged: true`. Add only the specific capabilities needed and set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`.
findings.falsePositives: Node-level system agents (CNI, storage drivers) that genuinely require it; keep them isolated.
findings.verification: Manifest has no `privileged: true`; workload still starts.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Public-read or public-write storage ACL
findings.description: A storage bucket ACL is set to a public canned ACL, exposing objects to anyone.
findings.remediation: Use `private`, enable block-public-access, and serve public assets through a CDN with origin access control.
findings.falsePositives: Buckets deliberately serving public static assets with no sensitive content.
findings.verification: ACL is private and public access block is enabled.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Shell command built from a dynamic string
findings.description: A shell is invoked with an interpolated or concatenated command string (or Python `shell=True`). Untrusted input can inject extra commands.
findings.remediation: Use an argument array without a shell: `execFile(cmd, [args])` in Node, `subprocess.run([cmd, *args])` in Python. Validate inputs against an allowlist.
findings.falsePositives: Fully constant commands. Interpolated values that are validated constants.
findings.verification: Command uses an argument array; a test confirms metacharacters are not interpreted.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: SQL query built with string concatenation or interpolation
findings.excerpt: db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + req.query.id);
findings.description: A SQL statement is assembled from variables instead of bound parameters, which can allow SQL injection when any value is user-controlled.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries or a query builder that binds values (`?`, `$1`, `%s` placeholders passed separately).
findings.falsePositives: Interpolated identifiers that come from a fixed allowlist, or constants.
findings.verification: Query text is a constant; values passed as parameters; test with a quote-containing input.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Dynamic code execution (eval / new Function / exec)
findings.description: Strings are compiled and executed as code. If any part is attacker-influenced this is remote code execution. This rule matches the call, not the data flow.
findings.remediation: Replace with a data-driven approach (lookup table, JSON.parse, ast.literal_eval). Never pass user input to an evaluator.
findings.falsePositives: Constant strings, build tooling, or sandboxed evaluators. Trace the argument to confirm.
findings.verification: The call is removed or its argument is proven constant; add a test with a malicious input.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Workflow grants write-all permissions
findings.description: `permissions: write-all` gives every job a token that can modify repository contents, packages and more.
findings.remediation: Declare `permissions: contents: read` at the top level and grant additional scopes per job only where required.
findings.falsePositives: None expected; the setting is explicit.
findings.verification: No `write-all` remains and the workflow still passes.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Container runs as root (no USER instruction)
findings.description: The Dockerfile never sets a non-root USER, so the final image runs as root by default. A compromise of the app gives root inside the container.
findings.remediation: Create an unprivileged user and add `USER <name>` before the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT.
findings.falsePositives: Images intentionally run as root for tooling or build-only stages.
findings.verification: `docker run --rm <image> id -u` returns a non-zero UID.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Remote script piped into a shell during build
findings.description: `curl|sh` or `wget|sh` executes whatever the remote server returns at build time, with no integrity check.
findings.remediation: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute. Prefer the distribution's package manager.
findings.falsePositives: Installers from a source you control and trust. Still no integrity verification.
findings.verification: No `| sh` / `| bash` remains; a checksum verification step precedes execution.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Security group or firewall open to the whole internet
findings.description: A Terraform rule allows 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0). Open ingress to administrative or database ports exposes them to internet scanning and attack.
findings.remediation: Restrict CIDR ranges to known addresses or place the service behind a load balancer, VPN or bastion.
findings.falsePositives: Intentionally public web ports (80/443) and egress rules. Review the port and direction.
findings.verification: Ingress CIDRs are restricted or documented as intentionally public.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Hardcoded credential assigned to a secret-named variable
findings.description: A variable or key named like a password, secret, token or API key is assigned a non-placeholder string literal.
findings.remediation: Treat the credential as compromised: revoke or rotate it at the issuer first, then remove it from the repository and load it from an environment variable or secret manager. Deleting it from the latest commit does not remove it from git history.
findings.falsePositives: Test data, example config, i18n labels. Values that look like placeholders, environment lookups or templates are skipped.
findings.verification: Re-run `vigilsutra audit` after removing the value; then confirm the credential was rotated at the issuer and review git history for earlier exposure.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: GitHub Action not pinned to a commit SHA
findings.description: A third-party action is referenced by a mutable tag or branch. If the tag is moved or the publisher is compromised, the workflow runs attacker-controlled code.
findings.remediation: Pin third-party actions to a full 40-character commit SHA and keep a trailing comment with the version. Use Dependabot or Renovate to update pins.
findings.falsePositives: First-party `actions/*` references are lower risk; local `./` actions and Docker digests are skipped.
findings.verification: Every `uses:` line for a non-local action ends in @<40 hex>.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: Base image uses :latest or no tag
findings.description: An unpinned base image changes without notice, which breaks reproducibility and can pull in vulnerable or malicious content.
findings.remediation: Pin to a specific version and, for production, an image digest (`image@sha256:…`).
findings.falsePositives: `FROM scratch` and references to earlier build stages are skipped.
findings.verification: Every FROM line has an explicit tag or digest.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).

findings.title: No security policy file found
findings.description: No SECURITY.md was found, so reporters have no documented way to disclose vulnerabilities privately.
findings.remediation: Add SECURITY.md with a private contact or GitHub private vulnerability reporting link and a response expectation.
findings.falsePositives: Policy kept in an org-level `.github` repository.
findings.verification: SECURITY.md exists at the repository root, `.github/` or `docs/`.
findings.mappingNote: CWE ids are orientation only, taken from the MITRE CWE list; no OWASP/NIST control mapping is asserted (mapping unverified).
